figures.caption: Figure 1. Through-Plane Cycling in LLZO with Operando Cross-Sectional Visualization Images, schematic, and electrochemical data from operando through-plane Li/LLZO/Li cell. (A) Schematic showing cell geometry. (B) Voltage response of cell during galvanostatic plating at 0.5 mA/cm2. (C) Postmortem image of active area of electrode interface that was plated into. (D–G) Image series from through-plane visualization of cell at times labeled in (B). (D) Before 0.5 mA/cm2 current pulse. (E) Just after nucleation. (F) As Li ﬁlaments reach half-way across the cell. (G) Just after short-circuit. See also Figure S1.

Figure 2. Demonstration of In-Plane Visualization Platform (A) Schematic representation of in-plane cell geometry and experimental setup. (B and C) images of in-plane Li/LLZO/Li cell before (B) and after (C) Li penetration and short-circuit. (D and E) Voltage response of cell during stepped current (D), with zoom-in shown in (E). (F) Nyquist plots of in-plane cell before and after cycling until short-circuit. (G) Image showing pellet with multiple in-plane cells deposited on the surface.

Figure 3. Different Types or Morphologies of Li Penetration Optical images ([A],[D], [G]), SEM images ([B], [E], [H]), and schematics ([C], [F], [L]) of straight Li-penetration type ([A]–[C]), branching type ([D]–[F]), spalling type ([G]–[I]), and diffuse type ([J]–[L]). Contrast and brightness adjustments were made to the entire image in (A) and (J) to make features more evident in in situ optical images.

Figure 4. Cross-Sectional Analysis of Branching-Type Li Filament Postmortem characterization of Li-penetration morphology with scanning electron and optical microscopy. Secondary [(A) and (D)] and backscattered (E) electron images of LLZO cross-section through branching-type Li ﬁlament at location shown in the optical images shown in (B). Optical image of same area of cross-section is shown in (C).

Figure 5. Cross-Sectional Analysis of Spalling-Type Li Filament Secondary [(A), (C), and (E)] and backscattered (B) electron images of FIB cross-sections through spalling-type Li ﬁlaments. Top-down (D) and cross- sectional (F) optical images of the same feature shown in (C).

Figure 6. Reversibility and Cyclability of Li Filaments: First Cycle (A and B) Optical image of in-plane Li/LLZO/Li cell at end of ﬁrst half-cycle at 75 mA/cm2 (A) and corresponding voltage trace (B). (C and D) Image during second half-cycle before Li is exhausted from ﬁlament structures on the left and corresponding voltage trace (D). (E and F) Image at point in second half-cycle when ﬁlament structures are exhausted of Li (disappear from view) (E) and corresponding voltage trace (F). (G and H) Image from end of second half-cycle (G) and corresponding voltage trace (H).

Figure 7. Reversibility and Cyclability of Li Filaments: Subsequent Cycles Voltage proﬁle of in-plane Li/LLZO/Li cell during galvanostatic cycling at 5 mA/cm2 and 10 mA/cm2 with points in time labeled (A), corresponding to the operando optical images in (B) to (L). (B) End of ﬁrst 5 mA/cm2 half-cycle, showing reversibility of Li penetration structures. (C) End of second half-cycle. (D) End of third half-cycle. (E) Beginning of ﬁrst 10 mA/cm2 half-cycle. (F) Middle of the same half-cycle. (G) End of the same half-cycle, showing dead Li formation. (H) Beginning of sixth half-cycle at 5 mA/cm2. (I) Middle of same half-cycle. (J) End of same half-cycle. (K) Middle of following half-cycle. (L) End of the same half-cycle.

Figure 8. Analysis of Li-Propagation Rate (A–C) Schematic representation of Li propagation and relaxation inside a crack (A). (B) shows Li penetration, and (C) shows Li extrusion. (D) Representative operando optical image of a Li-ﬁlled crack, with areas analyzed in (F) and Figures 9A and 9Blabelled accordingly. (E) Plot of crack growth over time during a representative set of current pulses. (F) Plot of pixel brightness versus position along a line across the crack tip for frames during and after a current pulse. (G) Plot of crack growth rate versus applied current. See also Figures S11 and S12.

Figure 9. Electron and Optical Microscopy Images of Straight-Type Crack Propagation (A and B) SEM image (A) and higher-magniﬁcation image (B) of Li that has been extruded out of the crack where it intersects the surface of the LLZO pellet. (C and D) Operando optical image (C) and higher-magniﬁcation image (D) of straight-type Li penetration. is strongly dependent on temperature and strain rate,38,39 because For this reason Li is susceptible to creep at room temperature, which would allow the Li within a crack to extrude backward when current is stopped. As further evidence of this behavior, Li that was extruded out of the crack is visible in postmortem SEM (Figures 9A and 9B). The relaxation is more dramatic at higher current densities. This is consistent with the fact that the strain rate in Li increases with current density, which leads to a higher stress accumulation at the crack tip.

Figure 10. Analysis of In-Plane Li/LLZO/Li Cell Behavior during Extended Galvanostatic Plating (A–C) Operando optical images at different points in time during Li plating. (D) Voltage response to the 4 mA/cm2 current pulses with inset showing voltage decay after the current pulses for selected pulses. (E) Area-speciﬁc resistance (based on the initial electrode areas) of interface, bulk, and total from EIS after each current pulse.
Figure 11. Cross-Sectional SEM Images of FIB-Cut Li/LLZO Interfaces (A) After stripping. (B) After plating.

figures.caption: Table S1. Table of parameters used for the COMSOL® model along with source of value. (Parameter | Value | Units | Description | Source) D_Li+ 2.8*10^-13 m2/s diffusivity of Li ions in LLZO (NMR, Hayamizu et al.); D_n 2*10^-15 m2/s diffusivity of negative ions in LLZO (extrapolated from high-temperature data, Kubicek et al.); C_Li+ 0.019675 mol/cm3 concentration of mobile Li ions (assuming half of Li sites are mobile); k_d 1.771*10^-4 s-1 dissociation rate constant (assumed from LiPON model); k_r 9*10^-9 m3/(mol-s) recombination reaction rate (assumed from LiPON model); j0 0.2 mA/cm2 exchange current density (data for Al-doped LLZO, Buschmann et al.); alpha 0.5 charge transfer coefficient (assumed).
